fetch-depth: 0 on both CI jobs, and INVALID now means the packet is wrong rather than the checkout was thin. The check separates a commit absent from this clone (UNVERIFIED, and the run says it is not ancestry evidence) from one absent from this repository (INVALID); a shallow clone under CI is itself a failure naming the workflow line, so deleting fetch-depth: 0 goes red again rather than passing having checked nothing. Proven both ways on GitHub Actions: run 30754387170 is the first green verify since 2026-08-01, reaching [state] valid then tsc then 58 test files; run 30755347566 was then made red on purpose with a fabricated commit sha and failed with the single line 'MAR-464: merged/proven commit 0badc0ffee... is not a commit in this repository', not the shotgun every-issue-INVALID a shallow clone produced. The break was reverted at b977a8e. tests/state-check.test.ts builds throwaway repositories for all four cases including the shallow-in-CI guard.

The cause is accumulated store state, and the path is exact. Proof 3h ends by writing a snapshot dated observed_at + 120s, deliberately, and nothing removed it; putAgentDomState refuses any snapshot older than the newest the runner has said, so for two minutes afterwards the next run's seed was refused as out of order and every proof from 3c down ran against the previous run's world. The intermittency was a stopwatch, not a race. It is NOT decisionIdentity treating runs[].progress or current_step as a change, and not a second writer for synthetic-gmail-meeting-assistant; MAR-464's fix is intact and tests/snapshot-carryover.test.ts rules that hypothesis out rather than assuming it away. Proof 3 now forgets the agent before seeding, 3i takes the fabricated future back out, and 3b asserts the seed was stored rather than merely accepted - an out-of-order snapshot is declined as { ok: true, superseded: true }, so reading only ok let the step report success having written nothing. The rollback guard is untouched and the new test holds it to that. Evidence: three consecutive pnpm verify:shell runs, 56 proofs each, zero failures. Runs 2 and 3 seeded 29.6s apart (15:52:24.275Z and 15:52:53.863Z), so run 3 sat inside the 120s window that used to poison it and would have been superseded under the old code.

Found while proving MAR-466, not filed before this session. tests/broker-transport.test.ts failed 3 runs out of 3 under full-suite load on Windows, on master's own code with none of this branch's changes, and passed in isolation and on Linux CI. settle(400) bet a fixed sleep on Windows spawning a Node process; the failures read 'expected [] to have a length of 1' - the child had not written yet. It now waits for the line rather than assuming it, accumulating across drains because a drain is destructive. Assertions unchanged and lib/broker/ untouched. Fixed here because pnpm verify could not go green on Windows without it. Three consecutive full-suite runs: 59 files, 1032 passed, 8 skipped, zero failures.

The cause is arithmetic, not luck, and the job logs settled it the way MAR-466's store row did. Across all 13 CI runs since 2026-08-01, telemetry propagation is a constant 3.3-5.5s while the agent's fetch is bimodal: ~1s when all three sources answer, 11-16s when one does not (items_total 30 vs 20). agent-kit/template/agent.mjs reads sources sequentially with a 15s timeout each, and 6g had a single 20s budget covering the fetch AND the propagation behind it, so one hung source spent 15 of the 20 and left ~5 for a step needing ~4. On 0ac58ac the fetch took 15.6s and the telemetry 4.6s: the gate lost by 0.2s and reported it as '6g ...: null'. The blocked-fetch story and the did-not-finish-in-the-wait story are the same event from two ends. Fixed by serving the mandatory gate three loopback feeds, one per parser; live sources moved to advisory 6l, which is dated, names the source that failed and can never fail a release. Three defects fixed independent of root cause: 6g reported null and now reports what it waited for, how long, over how many polls and what it saw; 6i/6j/6k cascaded off `completed?.run_id ?? ""` into three misleading red lines and now skip explicitly; 6j asserted only that a verdict existed, which passes on a zero-item digest from three dead sources, and twice did exactly that (runs 30736386756 and 30753436632 carried 20 items where 30 were expected) - it now asserts grounded AND 9 of 9 cited. 6m enforces ADR 0004 by reading the source addresses back out of the digest DASH received and failing if any is off-machine. Evidence: hosted Windows runner slack went from 4.4s on the failing run to ~20s (digest in 265ms vs 15.6s); pnpm verify green on Windows; CI green on three separate pushes to PR #32, the last of which is docs-only, the same commit shape that originally failed. Known unrelated flake: tests/broker-transport.test.ts 'drops past its bound' failed once in 5 full-suite runs under Windows load and passes in isolation - MAR-472's file, a different test, not fixed here. See ADR 0004.

DASH-28. Nothing distinguished 'quietly working' from 'died and nobody noticed': every existing signal (telemetry, the 5s Agent DOM poll, process facts) was evidence of activity, never an expectation of it. Design decision: trigger.schedule is free text ('weekdays at 08:00 local time') with no parseable structure, so deriving an expectation from it would mean parsing prose unreliably - added one small additive field instead, trigger.expected_interval_seconds, optional and meaningful only alongside type:schedule; absent means no derivable expectation and the agent is never marked stalled. stalled is deliberately NOT part of AgentStatus (the wire vocabulary an agent/runner may assert) but a new WorkspaceStatus = AgentStatus | 'stalled', computed only in lib/workspace.ts's buildOverview from timestamps the state snapshot already carries (runs/tasks/audit_events) - no new storage, no new polling, no runner changes. The killed-vs-quiet distinction the issue asks for falls out for free: runner/state.ts's existing resolveStatus already turns a confirmed-dead process into offline/error before DASH ever sees the snapshot, and the new derivation never overrides offline, error, paused, needs_attention, or an agent with an active run; a manual-trigger agent is exempt by construction. Surfaced on the workspace page (status, status_detail, next_action, new last_activity_at fact) and, separately, on the work inbox page as a 'May need a look' section - not folded into InboxItem, which is built around an expires_at a stalled agent doesn't have. Tests use fixed Date instants throughout, not wall-clock sleeps. Evidence: pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm test 60 files / 1065 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed. pnpm verify NOT run - Electron processes were already running on this machine from the concurrent MAR-469 session, and DASH is single-instance by design (MAR-450), so the real shell smoke was skipped rather than risking a collision. Merged to master in PR #36 (b778b23) on 2026-08-03.

tests/broker-transport.test.ts > 'drops past its bound rather than queueing unboundedly' failed once in five full-suite Windows runs during MAR-473's session and passed in isolation - the same class of defect MAR-472 fixed elsewhere in this file, on the one test MAR-472 did not convert. settle(700) bet a fixed sleep on Windows spawning a Node process and getting 200 written lines through the pipe within 700ms; under load the drain sometimes read dropped === 0 because nothing had overflowed yet. Converted to the file's waitUntil helper, polling until dropped > 0, copying the two adjacent tests MAR-467's session had already converted. The drop count accumulates across polls because a drain is destructive (MAR-472's reason); the request count does not accumulate the same way and is read from the latest drain only - accumulating it produced a real local failure (65 > 64) from an early poll draining a not-yet-full buffer before a later, separately-bounded drain added its own count on top, which would have been a false failure of a bound the code never actually violated. Assertions unchanged. tests/ only; lib/broker/ and runner/ untouched. Evidence: three consecutive full-suite runs on Windows, each 60 files / 1056 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed, plus a clean pnpm typecheck. pnpm verify was not run - not required for a tests-only change confined to this file. One CI run's shell-smoke check failed on an unrelated Windows EPERM cleanup race in a different proof's temp directory (dash-lapse-proof-*, part of MAR-467's work, nothing this branch touches); a rerun on the same commit passed clean, confirming it. PR open, not merged by this session.

ONE of the three cases is proven end to end and two are unit tests only; the split matters more than the total, and ADR 0005 records the judgment behind it. PROVEN END TO END on the installed shell (proof 8, using the issue's numbering): case 2, the request the runner destroyed because its bounded buffer was full. A real agent the runner spawned fired 200 brokered requests past a buffer of 64 and the shell's own broker loop drained, recorded and rendered them - 200 sent, 64 adjudicated, 136 dropped, identical in all three runs, so it is a bound being hit rather than a race. 8d is the load-bearing check: audit rows plus dropped requests may not exceed what the agent actually sent, which is exactly what a synthesised row would do, and a build that faked a plausible decision would pass every other check in the file and fail that one. 8e asserts the lapse carries no operation, decision or refusal; 8f asserts the rendered sentence names no operation either. UNIT TESTS ONLY: case 1 (DASH was closed) and case 3 (the answer DASH could not confirm was delivered). Case 3's runner half runs over the real local transport in tests/runner-server.test.ts and its DASH half - marking the right audit row - is in tests/broker-lapses.test.ts; what is not proven on the installed shell is the two halves meeting, because that needs a child to exit inside the window between DASH deciding and the runner writing. Case 1 cannot be driven by a proof running inside DASH, because it requires DASH not to be running; lib/broker/uptime.ts is tested exhaustively and the wiring in electron/main.ts is not covered by an installed proof. The issue's own account of case 3 was wrong and is corrected in ADR 0005: an undeliverable answer does not leave no trace, because lib/broker/execute.ts audits on every path before the answer travels, so the row already exists and overstates - it became a delivered column on the audit row rather than a second population of near-misses. The new broker_lapses table has no decision, refusal, operation, connection_id or request_id column and tests/store-sqlite.test.ts pins that list. Evidence: pnpm verify green on Windows at this tree - [state] valid, typecheck clean, 60 test files with 1056 passed and 8 skipped, and 63 installed-shell proof checks passed with zero failures plus one advisory note (6l, the live sources, which can never fail a release). Three smoke runs were triggered and the last two were green. The first failed 7d/7e/7f/7h/7i and the cause was inherited state, not this branch: a previous interrupted run had left its requests in the runner's bounded buffer, which survives DASH, and this pass drained them at startup (138 dropped, 64 undeliverable, both reported in the log), seeding the broker's per-agent replay set with proof 7's fixed request ids so this run's real calls came back duplicate_request. Proof 8 passed all six checks on that same first run. Proof 7's ids are now unique per smoke process, which is MAR-473's own lesson pointed the other way: a blocking gate that goes red for a reason unrelated to the change in hand teaches people to re-run it until it is green. See ADR 0005.

The remaining step to promote MAR-458 to proven: the same round trip against a real Google account rather than the loopback provider proof 7 binds. Needs a human at a consent screen, so it is a dated manual proof and must not be added to pnpm verify. Google Testing-mode data-scope grants expire after seven days, so record the date.

The permission broker's first slice. Raw access-token delivery is closed: deliverableSecretFields cannot return an OAuth target and assertNoBrokeredCredentials refuses the spawn if one appears. An agent invokes gmail.search and gmail.message.read, whose provider URL DASH constructs and whose response DASH projects, and writes a LOCAL draft artifact; no send operation and no provider-side draft creation exist, so gmail.compose grants nothing. A grant is the intersection of what DASH implements, what the manifest declared and what the provider issued, re-resolved on every call so a disconnect binds at the agent's next request. Not proven: the installed proof runs against a loopback provider because Google needs an account, a human at a consent screen and a restricted-scope verification DASH does not have, so proof 7 establishes the boundary and not Gmail's API. Also not done: the compiled Google client id is disclosed on the capability card rather than removed, and BYO-client onboarding stays where ADR 0002's rollout puts it. See ADR 0002 amendment 1, which corrects this ADR's own account of the defect.
